pairs.question: Quid uota furentem, quid delubra iuuant?
pairs.answer: Est mollis flamma medullas interea et tacitum uiuit sub pectore uulnus.
pairs.derivation: The poet asks what the prayers and shrines avail the raving Dido, then answers it himself: meanwhile the flame eats her soft marrow and the silent wound lives beneath her breast (i.e. they avail nothing). Question is the full interrogative at line 65-66. Answer ends at the first full stop (after uulnus); the preceding exclamation 'heu, uatum ignarae mentes!' (line 65) is framing/apostrophe and is dropped, and the following narration 'uritur infelix Dido...' begins a new sentence and is excluded. Stripped inline verse number 65 and the dangling 70/75 markers.
